title: Each trigger proposes a candidate; the earliest wins as the Due date
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a user with View customers, on the build under test.
  2. An asset is enrolled on a schedule whose service has more than one active trigger (e.g. a calendar interval and a mileage 'At' target), e.g. unit 'ZZAUTOTEST Truck 12'.
  3. Open the asset's Maintenance tab (the worklist and a work order's maintenance panel show the same rows).
custom_steps:
1. Find the service that has more than one trigger.
  2. Read the Due cell.
  3. Open the row menu and read the other candidates.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Every active trigger proposes a candidate date.
  • Due is the earliest candidate.
  • The Due cell shows that earliest candidate with its trigger; the row menu lists every other candidate with its date and trigger.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-3780 (Maintenance Reminders); story SV-10569 (S12, Due date resolution); Chunk 2 MR spec (Confluence 897679389), Part 2 / S12; read 2 Oct 2026. Source-verified 2 October 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S12-R1: “Every active trigger will propose a candidate date”
  • S12-R5: “Due will be the earliest candidate”
  • S12-R7: “Within one service, its triggers' candidates resolve to the earliest per S12-R5. The Due cell shows that one with its trigger per S9-R12, and the row menu lists every other candidate with its date and trigger. Rows are never merged across services on the asset tab, the worklist or the panel”
